fixer.title: mcp: fix local gateway disposal

introducer.title: mcp: initial data flow for MCP gateway

cases.mechanism: Each local gateway disposal previously sent `[gatewayId]` to a channel expecting `gatewayId`, causing cleanup to miss every string-keyed entry. One route and its event/session state remained per configured MCP server, and the HTTP listener could remain open until client disconnect or process shutdown; repeated create/dispose cycles accumulated this retained state.
cases.symptom: Disposed local gateways retained per-server routes, sessions and event listeners and continued processing server-change events; the gateway HTTP server also remained alive when these leaked routes were the last routes.
cases.fixedBehavior: The changed line calls the channel directly with the scalar gateway ID expected by McpGatewayChannel, allowing it to dispose the per-gateway event forwarder, remove client tracking, clean all per-server routes and sessions/listeners, and stop the shared HTTP server when the last route is gone.
cases.evidence: The base line invokes disposeGateway through ProxyChannel.toService. ProxyChannel.toService sends method arguments as an array (`channel.call(propKey, methodArgs)`), while McpGatewayChannel's manual `call` implementation casts its raw `args` to `string`. The resulting one-element array does not equal the string key used by `_gatewayDisposables`, `_clientGateways`, or McpGatewayService's `_gatewayRoutes`, so the service returns as an unknown gateway without running `_cleanupGateway`. The extension-host API reaches this path whenever a locally created McpGateway is disposed, via ExtHostMcp.dispose -> MainThreadMcp.$disposeMcpGateway -> result.dispose.

fixer.title: startup: Cache packaged ESM ASAR resolutions

fixer.title: authentication: release provider activation listeners

introducer.title: fix: race activateByEvent with provider registration to prevent auth deadlock

cases.mechanism: Timed-out provider activation attempts leave raceCancellation promises pending and retain one cancellation listener on the AuthenticationService lifetime token per attempt until service shutdown.
cases.symptom: Repeated requests for unavailable authentication providers accumulate listeners and retained promise closures for the lifetime of the workbench, eventually triggering listener-leak warnings and increasing memory/dispatch work.
cases.fixedBehavior: Each activation attempt now owns a linked CancellationTokenSource whose dispose(true) runs from tryActivateProvider's finally block. Successful registration, activation failure, and the 5-second timeout all cancel the operation token and remove the registrations from the long-lived service token, bounding retained listeners to currently active attempts.
cases.evidence: Before this change, tryActivateProvider passed the AuthenticationService lifetime token directly to raceCancellation. raceCancellation registers token.onCancellationRequested and disposes that registration only when its input promise settles or the token is cancelled. On the 5-second missing-provider timeout, Event.toPromise is disposed without settling, so providerRegistered remains pending and its cancellation listener remains attached until the whole service is disposed. getSessions/createSession and the declared-provider scan can invoke this path repeatedly; the added regression test exercises repeated missing-provider timeouts and verifies that listener-leak warnings no longer occur. The changed lines create a child source linked to the service token and register dispose(true) in the operation store, so finally cancellation settles raceCancellation and removes both its listener and the child source's parent listener.

fixer.title: Avoid synchronous activity bar size measurement

introducer.title: Support activity bar on top of primary side bar

cases.mechanism: A clientHeight geometry read of the rendered global action container ran synchronously inside every vertical Activity Bar layout, including the startup grid layout, and could flush pending style/layout work on the UI thread.
cases.symptom: Main-thread startup and resize layout latency from synchronous browser style/layout resolution in ActivityBarCompositeBar.layout.
cases.fixedBehavior: Vertical Activity Bar layout computes reserved global-action height from the two-action in-memory count and static action height/gap inputs, avoiding the synchronous DOM geometry read during startup and later layouts while retaining a single arithmetic calculation per layout.

Workbench layout constructs the Activity Bar as a grid leaf and workbenchGrid.layout invokes part layout on startup; ActivitybarPart.layout then calls ActivityBarCompositeBar.layout. The global action bar has already appended rendered action DOM, so this geometry read sits on the synchronous main-thread startup/layout path and can require style/layout resolution. The changed code replaces that read with GlobalCompositeBar.getHeight(actionHeight, actionGap), which uses the in-memory ActionBar length and the same sizing values published to CSS. Tests explicitly install a throwing clientHeight getter and verify all supported size/gap combinations, corroborating that the DOM measurement is no longer reached.

fixer.title: chat: reduce picker layout measurement work

introducer.title: chat input: refactor and responsiveness

cases.mechanism: The responsive chat picker layout sorted items by repeatedly reading live DOM geometry in the comparator and then reread every item's geometry for fit checks, multiplying synchronous layout-sensitive reads on startup, resize, and picker-content mutations.

In the base revision, _getOrderedVisibleItems filtered with getClientRects(), then its sort comparator called getBoundingClientRect() for both operands on every comparison; _fitsAvailableWidth subsequently measured every item again. fixer.title: Overlap macOS signing and notarization in official builds

introducer.title: Sign macOS server binaries

cases.mechanism: A global phase barrier serialized the start of every ESRP notarization behind completion of the slowest signing subprocess, leaving already-signed artifacts idle and making step latency max(all signing durations) plus max(all notarization durations) rather than the maximum per-artifact sign/notarize chain.
cases.symptom: Official macOS build completion was delayed whenever artifact signing durations differed, because notarization for early-finished artifacts could not overlap the remaining signing work.
cases.fixedBehavior: Each artifact now forms an independent sign-then-notarize chain, so a completed artifact enters the external notarization operation immediately instead of idling behind the slowest unrelated signing job. The total boundary-call count remains four operations for universal builds or eight for architecture-specific builds, and effective concurrency remains bounded by the two or four artifact chains.
cases.evidence: In the base revision, all 2 (universal) or 4 (architecture-specific) sign-darwin subprocesses were started, then every signing result was awaited through line 47 before the first notarize-darwin subprocess could be spawned at line 51. Each subprocess invokes the synchronous dotnet ESRP CLI path in build/azure-pipelines/common/sign.ts, and the encompassing Azure Pipelines Codesign & Notarize step cannot complete until all operations finish. The changed helper awaits only the matching artifact's signing operation before starting its notarization, and Promise.all retains parallel processing across independent artifacts.

fixer.title: sessions: address #335583 review feedback on ActionList hover panels

fixer.title: Batch SVG whitespace markers in the editor per line

cases.mechanism: The default SVG whitespace renderer created one SVG child element for every visible space or tab. Overlay line replacement on scrolling and selection-related rendering repeatedly constructed and destroyed a DOM subtree whose node count scaled with visible whitespace glyphs rather than visible lines.
cases.symptom: Editors with renderWhitespace enabled and whitespace-dense visible lines incurred excessive synchronous DOM/style recalculation during scrolling and drag selection, causing increased renderer task time and frame delays.

Rendering still scans and serializes each visible marker, but DOM element creation, attachment, style matching, and teardown shrink from one shape per whitespace glyph to at most one shape per rendered line.

ViewOverlays.prepareRender runs the overlay on invalidation, ViewOverlayLine concatenates its markup with the other overlays, and viewLayer applies changed line HTML through innerHTML, making all of those glyph nodes synchronous DOM/style work during visible-line rendering. The PR body provides controlled editor measurements showing 778 glyph elements before versus 49 per-line paths after and corresponding reductions in selection and scrolling style-recalculation time.

fixer.title: Reuse text buffers in chat edits for checkpoint replay

introducer.title: refactor: edit operations timeline

cases.mechanism: Checkpoint replay rebuilt and reserialized the entire text buffer for every recorded text-edit operation, producing O(K*N)-style full-document CPU/allocation work for K small batches over a large file and blocking undo, redo, restore, and cold snapshot/diff model creation.
cases.symptom: Large chat-edited files with many recorded edit operations can freeze or substantially delay checkpoint undo/redo/restore and cold historical diff rendering because repeated full-document scans and copies execute before those actions complete.
cases.fixedBehavior: The added contiguous TextEdit grouping applies all version-ordered edit batches to one PieceTreeTextBuffer and extracts content only once per ordinary-text run, reducing full-buffer construction/extraction from one per edit operation to one per run while retaining create/delete/rename and notebook boundaries and disposing the buffer in finally.
cases.evidence: Before this PR, _replayOperations awaited _applyOperationToState once for every TextEdit operation; that branch called _applyTextEditsToContent for each operation. _applyTextEditsToContent calls createTextBuffer on the complete current content, whose createTextBufferFactory passes the entire string to PieceTreeTextBufferBuilder.acceptChunk/createLineStarts, and then extracts the complete resulting string. The path is directly awaited by undoInteraction/redoInteraction/restoreSnapshot through navigateToCheckpoint, and by snapshot-model creation used for diff rendering. Thus K edit batches over a document of size N repeatedly scan and materialize the full document on the renderer-side critical path. The PR's tests also establish the old multiplicity versus the fixed invariant by asserting one buffer creation/disposal for multiple edit operations.

cases.fixedBehavior: On every HydraFusion create/resume without an explicit tool filter, the launcher passes HYDRAFUSION_DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_TOOLS to the SDK, preventing 42 VS Code-only tool schemas from being serialized into repeated model requests while preserving explicit user overrides.
cases.evidence: Commit 31671b1f50693b2b9f551f72b519c3afe225990a introduced the selectable HydraFusion model. In the base launcher, absent a user override, excludedTools stayed undefined and the generic runtime registered the full client/server/extension tool set into the SDK session. The changed path now selects a 42-name HydraFusion denylist and forwards it through ResumeSessionConfig.excludedTools. The PR's measured comparison reports HydraFusion request input falling from 44.0K to 27.6K tokens and AIC/task from 74.9 to 56.4, consistent with the code comment identifying roughly 13K tool-definition tokens per request.

fixer.title: extensions: keep update checks on polling cadence

introducer.title: extensions: add delayed auto-update mode to extensions.autoUpdate

cases.mechanism: Each earliest quarantine expiry initiated another full installed-extension update check outside the normal cadence. For N installed extensions this repeated O(N) metadata and synchronization work and could launch N concurrent latest-version HTTP GETs, or a grouped marketplace query POST.
cases.symptom: Quarantine expiry caused an additional marketplace update-check burst, increasing network traffic and CPU/serialization beyond the regular polling cadence.
cases.fixedBehavior: Removing the expiry timer keeps full marketplace checks on the existing 12-hour scheduler, avoiding the extra full synchronization and network burst when an extension becomes eligible.
cases.evidence: Deleted base line 2306 scheduled eventuallyCheckForUpdates(true) at the earliest delay expiry. That cancels the cadence delayer, immediately runs checkForUpdates(), builds infos for all installed extensions, and calls galleryService.getExtensions(infos). The resource API uses Promise.all over those infos and sends a GET per UUID-backed extension; its fallback sends a grouped query POST. The added fake-timer test counts getExtensions and proves that crossing expiry no longer adds a check, while the unchanged scheduler still checks every 12 hours.

fixer.title: Fix browser double-navigating pages opened via `window.open`

introducer.title: Refactor agentic browser opening lifecycle

cases.mechanism: Every allowed window.open popup previously combined Chromium's navigation of the returned WebContents with a second explicit WebContents.loadURL of the same URL, repeating page fetch, document parsing, lifecycle events, and associated subresource work once per popup.
cases.symptom: Pages opened through window.open were navigated twice, causing duplicate network/page-load work and added popup-open latency; for about:blank popups subsequently populated with document.write, the extra load also replaced the initial document.
cases.fixedBehavior: Popup WebContents supplied by Electron no longer receive an additional explicit loadURL; Chromium completes the original window.open navigation once. Child views without supplied WebContents still receive their initial URL through the existing loadURL path.
cases.evidence: In the base revision, BrowserView.setWindowOpenHandler passes Electron's existing popup WebContents and details.url into _createChildView (browserView.ts:187-226). The callback at browserViewMainService.ts:431-439 always copied that URL to initialUrl, and _createBrowserView then unconditionally invoked view.loadURL(initialUrl) at lines 477-481. Electron also completes the original window.open navigation after createWindow returns the same WebContents, so the base path issued a second navigation for each allowed popup. The changed line gates initialUrl when electronOptions.webContents exists, while preserving explicit loading for child views created without existing WebContents (browserView.ts:769).

fixer.title: agent Host: Reduce redundant Git work in AH sessions

introducer.title: AgentHost - add multi-root support for the checkpoint service

cases.mechanism: Multi-root checkpoint loops repeated full Git working-tree capture and commit/ref work for every configured folder even when several folders shared one checkout root.
cases.symptom: Turn-start and turn-end checkpoint latency scaled with folder count rather than unique repositories, adding repeated Git subprocess and filesystem work for common multi-folder sessions.
cases.fixedBehavior: Successful baseline, turn-start, and turn-end captures now mark the resolved repository root complete and skip additional folders resolving to that same root, reducing expensive working-tree snapshots and commit/ref subprocesses from O(folders) to O(unique checkout roots) per capture phase.
cases.evidence: The base implementation iterated every configured working directory and invoked _writeCheckpointCommit for each. That helper calls captureWorkingTreeAsTree, which runs git status/rev-parse/index discovery and may create a temp index and run additional Git commands. Multiple workspace folders can resolve to the same checkout root; the added ResourceSet guard at RIGHT:75 makes each successful repository capture occur once per phase while the new tests prove retries remain possible after failure and later turns still take fresh snapshots.

fixer.title: chat: polish progress and inline tool rendering

introducer.title: chat: improve Draw persistent progress animation

cases.mechanism: Every visible animation frame rebuilt identical full-band geometry and long SVG path strings for marks wholly inside the revealed ribbon interval.
cases.symptom: The Draw animation incurred avoidable geometry CPU and string allocations at display-frame frequency; the new finite cache removes the unchanged portion of that work.
cases.fixedBehavior: Fully covered marks now reuse one of four cap-specific path strings from a bounded cache, while only genuinely moving endpoints call strip.
cases.evidence: ChatWorkingLogo calls getChatWorkingLogoDrawFrame from a recursive requestAnimationFrame loop. In the base revision, Ribbon.bands generated each visible mark by calling strip on every moving frame, including fully covered marks whose geometry and cap flags were unchanged. fixer.title: github: avoid throttling generic 403 denials

introducer.title: Back off GitHub requests instead of hammering a failing service

cases.mechanism: A generic authorization denial was stored as a negative cooldown entry, delaying all later requests for the same account/resource for at least 60 seconds despite healthy quota.
cases.symptom: After a generic 403 containing "Rate Limit Exceeded", otherwise valid REST, GraphQL, download, or bootstrap work for the same quota bucket could remain queued or time out behind an invented 60-second cooldown.
cases.fixedBehavior: The shared classifier now accepts a generic 403 body only when exhausted-quota or Retry-After evidence exists, or when the explicit "API rate limit exceeded" message has no usable remaining-quota feedback. Healthy-quota generic denials remain authorization failures and no longer create the 60-second queued-request delay.
cases.evidence: In the base revision, line 107 classified any HTTP 403 body containing "rate limit" as throttling. updateFromResponse then assigned the unhinted 60,000 ms blockedUntil, CooldownState.getDelay exposed that delay, and RequestQueue skipped matching account/resource requests until its wake timer. The added bootstrap test exercises the concrete trigger—a 403 body "Rate Limit Exceeded" with x-ratelimit-remaining: 4999—and verifies that subsequent requests should dispatch without a cooldown.

fixer.title: Improve Copilot Agent Host sandbox controls and policy display

introducer.title: Add sandbox policy reports to Copilot agent sessions

cases.mechanism: Each command invocation allocated and retained a new directory plus Markdown file until explicit session deletion, causing filesystem bytes and inode count to grow linearly with policy-report history even after the live session was disposed.
cases.symptom: Repeated policy checks accumulated persistent report snapshots and directory entries, increasing session storage and later filesystem traversal/deletion work with the number of invocations.
cases.fixedBehavior: The changed line uses the stable per-session `diagnostics/sandbox-policy.md` path, so each successful invocation replaces the prior report and bounds retained report files to one per session.
cases.evidence: The base line created a fresh UUID directory for every successful `/sandbox policy` invocation, and the adjacent write stored a full Markdown report there. Session data lives under persistent `agentSessionData/<session>` and is deleted only when the session itself is deleted; disposing the live session does not remove those snapshots. The changed test explicitly exercises two invocations followed by session disposal and now expects one latest file. Blame identifies c0f6c8cd52aeceb78b91631bce1b37d161a93d3f as introducing the UUID path.

fixer.title: agentHost: Enable artifact tools by default

introducer.title: agentHost: Restrict automatic PR association

cases.mechanism: With automatic association enabled, every accepted turn ends by calling `attachSessionGitHubPullRequest`; on a non-base branch with no PR, the resolver performs a GitHub head-branch query (and potentially a local `rev-parse` plus SHA query), but a miss does not record a negative result, so the next turn repeats the same lookup.
cases.symptom: Repeated background GitHub requests and local Git work after each completed turn on feature branches that do not yet have a pull request.
cases.fixedBehavior: Defaulting automatic attachment off routes sessions through restricted reconciliation. With no recorded or explicitly associated PR candidates, `_canReuseResolution` completes without calling `resolveForCheckout`, eliminating the per-turn GitHub lookup for the default Stable scenario.
cases.evidence: `GitHubReferencesContribution.onTurnEnd` invokes attachment after every non-rejected turn. `_attachSessionGitHubPullRequest` in automatic mode calls `resolveForCheckout` whenever `pullRequestBranchName` does not equal the current branch; on a miss it returns without setting that branch marker. The test `keeps the known pull request but resumes looking after the branch changed` explicitly expects two calls for two attempts while the first has no PR. The changed default at line 207 selects restricted mode, whose zero-candidate path returns before network resolution.

fixer.title: agentHost: keep WSL sessions after a successful launcher exit

introducer.title: agentHost: fix SSH and WSL relay reuse on reconnect

cases.mechanism: The normal detached-launcher exit was treated as backend failure, closing live relay leases and causing each recovery to repeat WSL detection and bootstrap subprocess work.
cases.symptom: Successful WSL agent-host launches immediately lost their reusable session and forced avoidable WSL subprocess/bootstrap work and reconnection latency.
cases.fixedBehavior: A code-0 launcher exit after readiness no longer tears down the per-distro session or relay leases, so later connects reuse the detached host URL and avoid repeated WSL platform detection/bootstrap subprocesses.
cases.evidence: In the base revision, every child `exit` called `onChildFailure`; after the URL had produced a session, that path called `_closeSession`, disposed every relay, and forced the next `connect`/`reconnect` through `_connectUnguarded`, including `_resolvePlatform` (`wsl uname`), a new `wsl.exe` bootstrap process, and a new WebSocket. The changed guard at line 394 recognizes the launcher's documented normal code-0 exit after printing the detached host URL. The added lifecycle tests exercise exits before, during, and after relay acquisition and prove subsequent connect/reconnect reuse one spawn rather than bootstrap again.

fixer.title: agentHost: avoid redundant changeset operation refreshes

introducer.title: AgentHost - adopt the ChangesetContentChanged action

cases.mechanism: A session-level refresh synchronously recomputed and published an operations action for every subscribed changeset even when all computed operation arrays were unchanged, multiplying state-envelope and downstream serialization/consumer work by subscription count.
cases.symptom: Workspace/configuration and operation-provider events in a 32-chat session with 804 subscriptions could publish hundreds of redundant unchanged operation envelopes, causing avoidable CPU/IPC fan-out and latency.
cases.fixedBehavior: The new helper compares the computed operation list with the changeset's current operations and returns before dispatching an unchanged action; event-triggered refresh requests are also coalesced per microtask and owner, bounding duplicate computations within one burst.
cases.evidence: Base line 274 unconditionally dispatches ChangesetOperationsChanged after every operation recomputation. updateOperations(session) expands through _getOperationOwners to each chat/folder owner and then every subscribed changeset. The added large-session test establishes a realistic 32-chat/804-subscription workspace-change scenario and asserts that unchanged operation state previously reached this publication path; the new _dispatchOperationsChanged equality guard suppresses those unchanged actions. Blame identifies the unconditional publication as introduced by fe9f87ca05dca0086aabaf24c7ffaf33888e2a1d.
